changelog: feat: the three things the BI report does that we could not. (1) GROUP MEANS, not just facets. 'Columns: one per sample / group mean' on every taxonomy bar and taxonomic heatmap. Faceting puts a group's samples side by side in a panel; the report's 'by Breeding' and 'by Region' figures are the MEAN of each group, one bar per group, which is a different figure and the one that gets read when the question is Cattle versus Buffalo rather than these 34 animals. Hidden samples are dropped before the mean is taken - a sample switched off must not keep contributing - and the top taxa are re-ranked on the group means, so the colours describe the chart on screen. Faceting is withdrawn in this mode because the columns already are the groups. The table view aggregates with it, so the two can never disagree. (2) NO NAME IS SHORTENED IN AN EXPORTED FIGURE. The legend used to cut every entry at 26 characters, so the PNG read 'Christensenellaceae R-7 g...' - a key that cannot be used, in the file that is the deliverable. The report figure is now sized around its legend instead of the legend being cropped to the figure: the longest name is measured, the entries are laid out in as many columns as fit between the title and the foot, and the canvas grows until every one has a place. Growth goes into width first and height after three columns, and the plot area keeps at least 680px so the bars are not narrowed to make room for their own key. The screen legend still clips, because the panel width is fixed there and the full name is in the tooltip and the table. (3) Top 40 and Top 50 are selectable, which is what the report uses. Tests: 13 drivers, 434 checks, including the real U2Bio-139-v144Genus result folder. Still missing against that report, and worth saying plainly rather than discovering later: annotation strips above the heatmaps and the beta-distance heatmap, PCoA and UPGMA coloured by group, rarefaction curves summarised per group with a ribbon, alpha-diversity boxplots faceted by metric, the prevalence-versus-abundance plot, and a saved settings profile that can be reused across jobs.
